newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Coffee seen slightly oversold, up near-term.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Coffee seen slightly oversold, up near-term.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
LIFFE coffee futures dipped into oversold territory, which could mean further near-term gains as the market corrects the condition, analysts said.
July was called to open $20 to $30 higher to extend Monday's rebound from the lowest level since May 14 hit on Friday.
"In the very near-term, the bias is to the upside," said independent technical analyst Elli Gifford. "The market is becoming oversold but not dramatically considering how overbought it was."

Gifford also noted that September's sharp fall last week helped to contract complete a 61.8-percent retracement of its earlier move up, which should mean coffee was ready to resume its climb. She said weekly coffee charts were still in a strong bull trend.
Strong September support rests at $1,825 per tonne, which goes back to highs made earlier this year, she said.
Initial September resistance was pegged at $1,925 and $2,000. But strong resistance was seen in a band between $2,025 and $2,300.
